title: Zero probability of reaching an inaccessible vertex
statement: Let $V=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and let $r$ be a symmetric relation on $V$. Suppose vertices $s,t\in V$ are such that there is no finite sequence of $r$-steps from $s$ to $t$, allowing a sequence of length zero. Let $D\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $n\le D$, let $b\in\mathbb{N}$, and fix a bijection from Boolean strings of length $b$ to $\{0,\ldots,D-1\}$. Form the $D$-slot graph on $V$ by using each slot to move along its corresponding $r$-edge when that edge exists, and otherwise leaving the vertex unchanged. For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, if a uniformly random Boolean string of length $kb$ is split into $k$ consecutive blocks of length $b$ and decoded as slot choices, the probability that the resulting walk starting at $s$ visits $t$ is zero.
hypotheses_covered: $s,t\in V$ and $t$ is not reachable from $s$ by any finite sequence of $r$-steps, including a sequence of length zero
